title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Game Days, Runbooks, Postmortems, and Communication Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's standard process for on-call rotations, incident detection and triage, runbook usage, postmortem expectations, game day exercises, and customer-facing communications (status page and templates). It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and incident commanders. Follow the procedures here for any production-impacting event affecting latency, availability, correctness, or data integrity.

Scope

- Services covered: inference-gateway, model-router, kv-cache-service, batching-service, telemetry-ingest, dedicated-proxy and associated infra (DBs, message queues).
- Environments: prod, prod-staging (for rehearsals).
- Audience: on-call engineers, incident commanders (IC), support, product and customer-facing roles.

High-level incident lifecycle

1) Detection & Alerting
   - Alerts originate from monitoring (Prometheus/Thanos, synthetic checks), tracing anomalies (Jaeger), logs (ELK), and customer reports (Support Zendesk).
   - Alerts are routed through PagerDuty with service-specific escalation policies.

2) Triage
   - First responder acknowledges in PagerDuty within the SLA window (see PagerDuty escalation matrix).
   - If the cause is not immediately known within 10 minutes, escalate to the next on-call and notify the IC.

3) Containment & Mitigation
   - Apply runbook steps to mitigate user-visible impact (traffic reroutes, scale up, failover to canary model variants, temporary rate limits).

4) Recovery
   - Confirm system is healthy (end-to-end synthetic checks green, error rates < SLO thresholds, user-facing latency within SLO).

5) Post-incident analysis & follow-up
   - IC files a postmortem within 72 hours (initial draft) and a final postmortem within 7 days.
   - Action items must have an owner and deadline and be tracked in JIRA.

Incident severity taxonomy (how we categorize incidents)

- Sev 0 (P0): Service-wide outage or data loss with major customer impact (SLO breach affecting >50% customers or critical revenue paths). Immediate executive notification.
- Sev 1 (P1): Degraded service impacting a significant subset of traffic (e.g., inference latency > 3x SLO for 30+ minutes, or embeddings generation failing for a tier). PagerDuty IC.
- Sev 2 (P2): Localized degradation or non-critical regression (increased error rate for a small service, intermittent failures). Triage by on-call.
- Sev 3 (P3): Minor issues, operational tasks, or internal infra improvements. Address via normal backlog.

Service Level Objectives and alert thresholds (examples)

- API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly; alert at 99.9% rolling 1h and 99.5% 24h.
- 95th percentile token latency (generation): < 300ms for small models; alert at >450ms sustained 15m.
- Error rate (5xx): alert if >1% sustained over 5m or >0.5% for 30m.
- Synthetic health check failure: alert if >3 regions fail simultaneously for 2 consecutive checks.

Roles and responsibilities

- First responder (on-call engineer): Acknowledge alert, follow runbook, collect diagnostics, escalate if needed.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates response, communications, and major mitigation decisions.
- Secondary on-call / escalation: Provides additional debugging and system knowledge.
- Communications lead (Comms): Drafts customer-facing messages and updates status page. Usually a support/product representative.
- Postmortem author(s): IC + primary engineers who worked incident; coordinates follow-ups.

PagerDuty & escalation matrix (summary)

- Primary on-call: 0-15 minutes to acknowledge. If no ack, page secondary on-call after 5 minutes.
- Secondary on-call: respond within 10 minutes of receiving escalation.
- IC escalation: If incident is P0/P1 and unresolved after 15 minutes, IC is engaged automatically.
- Executive notification: For P0, on-call must notify VP of Eng and Head of Customer Success within 30 minutes.

On-call rotations

- Team-owned rotations are maintained in PagerDuty and mirrored in the oncall calendar. Each rotation entry includes name, start/end time, backup, and escalation contacts.
- Typical rotation: 1 week primary rotation per team member with 24/7 coverage supported by follow-the-sun cross-team escalations.
- Handoff checklist (every shift):
  1. Verify PagerDuty schedule and contact info.
  2. Read last 24h incident summaries in #oncall-briefing channel.
  3. Check synthetic dashboards and outstanding maintenance tasks.
  4. Confirm laptop VPN/KMS access and SSH keys for oncall tools.

Runbook structure & best practices

Every runbook should include the following flat fields as a page header and then steps:
- Service name
- Owning team
- PagerDuty escalation
- Expected symptoms
- Impact assessment guidance
- Safety checks and preconditions
- Step-by-step mitigation steps (numbered)
- Verification steps
- Rollback guidance (if applicable)
- Post-incident artifacts to collect (logs, traces, configs)

Sample runbook excerpt:

Service: inference-gateway
Owning team: eng-serving-runtime
Symptoms: 5xx errors on /v1/generate, elevated request queue depth, 95th percentile generation latency > 600ms

Mitigation steps:
1) Check service health: `kubectl -n production get pods -l app=inference-gateway` and `kubectl describe pod <pod>` for OOM/killing.
2) Inspect fleet metrics: open Grafana dashboard `infra/inference-gateway` (panels: 5xx-rate, queue-depth, cpu/gpu-util).
3) If pods are OOM or CPU starved, scale replica count: `kubectl scale deploy inference-gateway --replicas= N` (follow autoscaler guidance).
4) If downstream model nodes are saturated, toggle routing policy to fallback model-variant: `curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/routing/override -d '{"service":"inference-gateway","route":"fallback-small"}'` (IC approval required for >10% traffic change).
5) If problem persists, enable temporary rate-limiting in gateway: update config map `gateway-config` -> `route.rate_limit: 100rps` and roll out.

Verification: Synthetic checks green, 5xx rate back to baseline, 95p latency within usual SLO for 15 minutes.

Postmortem template (required fields)

- Title (1 line)
- Incident ID (generated)
- Severity
- Start / end timestamps (UTC)
- Impact summary (customer-facing effect + number of customers affected)
- Timeline (bullet list with timestamps and short description)
- Root cause (concise)
- Contributing factors (list)
- Mitigation & recovery actions (what we did)
- Long-term fixes / action items (owner + due date)
- Detection & escalation analysis (what alerted, where delays happened)
- Lessons learned & follow-ups
- Attachments: logs, dashboards, traces, pager duty logs

Postmortem expectations

- Initial draft within 72 hours, final postmortem with assigned action items within 7 days.
- Action items are tracked in JIRA with proper labels (incident-YYYYMMDD, sevX).
- Postmortems are public to the company unless customer-sensitive; if sensitive, mark confidentiality and redaction notes.

Game days (rehearsal process)

Purpose: validate runbooks, rotations, and communications under simulated incidents.

Game day cadence & roles:
- Frequency: quarterly per team and annually cross-functional (engineering + support + product).
- Organizer: Eng SRE.
- Participants: on-call, secondary, IC, comms lead, support.

Sample game day scenario:
1) Inject synthetic 5xx flood to inference-gateway in prod-staging during the exercise window.
2) Trigger a failing synthetic check and observe PagerDuty wake-up.
3) Time to ack, time to mitigation, and time to recovery are recorded.
4) After-action review (AAR) within 48 hours: what worked, gaps in runbook, communication delays.

Metrics to measure from game days:
- Time-to-ack, time-to-mitigate, time-to-recover
- Number of missed runbook steps
- Quality of customer comms (measured via template adherence checklist)

Status page & customer communication templates

Status page policy:
- The status page (status.redwood.ai) is the single source of truth for customer-facing incident status.
- Updates must be posted within 30 minutes of incident classification as P1/P0 and every 30 minutes thereafter until recovery.

Template: initial customer-facing status update (use for P1/P0)

Title: Major service degradation affecting text generation
Impact: We are currently experiencing elevated error rates and increased latency for text-generation requests. A subset of customers may see failures or degraded performance.
What we're doing: Our engineers are investigating and have implemented temporary mitigations (traffic re-routing and throttling) while we identify the root cause.
Next update: We will post updates every 30 minutes or as significant progress is made.

Template: follow-up update

Title: Progress update — mitigation in place
Impact: The temporary mitigation has reduced the error rate by ~70% and latency is trending toward normal. Some customers may still experience degraded performance.
What we did: Enabled fallback routing to smaller model variant, scaled inference-fleet by +25%.
What we're doing next: Continue root cause analysis and gradually restore original routing once confidence checks pass.
Next update: in 30 minutes.

Template: incident resolved

Title: Incident resolved — service restored
Impact: All services are restored to normal levels. No data loss observed.
What we did: Reverted temporary routing and scaled back fleet. Final verification through synthetic checks and customer transaction tests passed.
Follow-up: We will publish a postmortem with timeline and action items within 7 days.

Internal communication guidance

- Channel: #incidents (Slack) for coordination; #oncall-briefing for summaries; #exec-ops for executive notifications.
- Use subject tags: [INCIDENT][SEV1] short-title.
- IC posts hourly internal updates for P1/P0 and documents shift handoffs.

Customer comms best practices

- Be transparent: state impact, what we are doing, and expected updates.
- Avoid speculation about root cause until confirmed.
- If a customer reaches out directly, route to support with the incident ID and status page link.

Tools & artifacts to collect during incident

- PagerDuty incident log export (timestamps, acks, escalations).
- Grafana dashboard snapshots and Prometheus queries used.
- Jaeger traces for sample failing request IDs.
- Kubernetes pod logs and node metrics.
- Control-plane config versions (model routing, feature flags).

Runbook hygiene & maintenance

- Owners must review runbooks quarterly or after any incident for which the runbook was used.
- Label runbook pages with last-reviewed date in the header (e.g., last_reviewed: 2026-02-10).
- Remove deprecated runbooks and replace cross-references.

Appendices

A — Quick commands (auth and tooling)
```
# Check PD incident status
pdctl incidents list --service inference-gateway

# Retrieve recent 5xx logs from Kibana
kibana-query "service:inference-gateway AND status:500" --last 30m

# Temporary routing override (requires IC token)
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/routing/override -H "Authorization: Bearer $IC_TOKEN" -d '{"service":"inference-gateway","route":"fallback-small"}'
```

B — Example Slack notification (internal)

[INCIDENT][SEV1] inference-gateway - Elevated 5xx rate
Impact: Elevated 5xxs for /v1/generate (~25% of requests), user-facing latency increased.
IC: @Ravi_Srinivasan
On-call: @oncall-inference
Status: Investigating — fallback routing applied. Next update in 30 minutes.

C — Postmortem checklist
- [ ] Draft posted to confluence within 72 hours
- [ ] Attach logs, dashboards, and PagerDuty audit
- [ ] Convert action items into JIRA tasks with owners and due dates
- [ ] Schedule follow-up review meeting if action items exceed 3 weeks

D — Glossary
- IC: Incident Commander
- SLO: Service Level Objective
- PD: PagerDuty
- AAR: After Action Review
